Now when I put all the variables into a multivariate model, the 95% quantile of parameters of some variables contain 0. Is there a ways to do backward elimination in the INLA package?

Thanks!

Ma Ho

messages.body_plain:
On 12/03/2013 06:39 PM, Havard Rue wrote:
> For many fixed effects, it can be easier (?) to keep the formula, like
>
> 	y � 1 + X
>
> where X is a matrix with the fixed effects as the columns and appropriate column names.
> then you can just change matrix X and keep the formula constant.
>
> H

yes!

it can be used to reduce the loop levels. Taking a look on the code that
I send in previous e-mail, it still wrong... At each level a new formula
object need to be created as the previous one updated.

Using the Havard idea we have:

n <- 100; p <- 3; set.seed(123)
X <- cbind(1, matrix(runif(n*p), n))
colnames(X) <- paste('x', 0:p, sep='')
s = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=0.9), sd=0.5)
u = rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)
z <- runif(n)
s.z = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=0.7), sd=0.3)
y = X%*%c(-1:1,0) + u + s + z*s.z

round(coef(summary(lm(y~0+s+ssz+X,
                       data.frame(y,s,ssz=s.z*z,X)))), 4)

jx = cbind(1, as.matrix(do.call('expand.grid',
     lapply(1:p, function(p) 0:1))))

file.res <- '~/dic-all-models.txt'
cat('s','sz', colnames(X)[-1], 'dic\n', file=file.res)
form0 = y ~ 0 + ff

require(INLA)

for (s in 0:1) {
     form.s = form0
     if (s==1)
         form.s = update(form0, '.~.+f(s, model="ar1")')
     for (sz in 0:1) {
         form.sz <http://form.sz> = form.s
         if (sz==1)
             form.sz <http://form.sz> = update(form.sz <http://form.sz>, '.~.+f(sz, z, model="ar1")')
         for (j in 1:nrow(jx)) {
             dtemp <- list(y=y, s=1:n, sz=1:n, z=z,
                           ff=X[,which(jx[j,]==1)])
             res = inla(form.sz <http://form.sz>, data=dtemp,
                 control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))
             cat(s, sz, jx[j,-1], res$dic$dic,
                 '\n', file=file.res, append=TRUE)
             cat(s, sz, jx[j,-1], res$dic$dic, '\n')
         }
     }
}

ddic = read.table(file.res, header=TRUE)
fo = update(dic ~ s + sz,
  paste('.~.+', paste(colnames(X)[-1], collapse='+')))
round(coef(summary(lm(fo, ddic))), 4)

instead.  For example:

so that should show you if there are any _non_-NA/NaN in the variable.
If there are no regular values in it, it can't be plotted,
and you'll need to go back to the model&inla call to see why that happens.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error when plotting predicted mean
messages.body_plain:
This is not an error in fact. The message says that you specify the data but it is not used. To understand it, is necessary to understand how R works with '=' and '<-' to.

Your code:

> print(levelplot(row.values=proj.grid$x,column.values=proj.grid$y,
> + x=pred.mean1,
> + col.regions<-tim.colors(64),
> + xlim=c(0.1707613,15.9874216),ylim=c(11.70414,23.52080),
> + aspect="iso",
> + xlab="Easting",ylab="Northing"))

one can says "There is no specification of the 'data' argument!" But, in fact yes!

When you do
 levelplot(..., col.regions <- a,  )
by using '<-' inside the () on a function call, you aren't passing 'a' for 'col.regions' argument. Because you specify the first argument, 'x', explicitely, 'a' is assumed as the value for 'data', the second argument. It is assigned to 'data' because it is the first unspecified argument.
